title: Support air-gapped backup artifact import/export (offline mode + local checksum verification)
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Private installer: add offline import/export helpers for backup artifacts (air-gapped). Includes local SHA256 verification, path safety checks, and docs for deterministic bundle layout.
body: ## Summary This PR adds first-class support for moving backup artifacts into/out of air-gapped environments with deterministic, locally verifiable integrity checks. It introduces: (1) `backup export` to package a previously created backup artifact + manifest into a portable bundle directory (or tar), (2) `backup import` to ingest a bundle into an air-gapped target cluster/operator workstation without any outbound calls, and (3) an explicit `--offline` mode that hard-fails if code paths attempt network access (including accidental cloud metadata calls). The goal is to enable on-prem/air-gapped customers to follow a repeatable workflow: create backup -> export to removable media -> import on restore site -> restore apply. Related: ENG-9829 (air-gapped bundle signing/verification follow-ups), ENG-9821 (`backup create`), customer issue context in SUP-18477 (restore failures due to missing/incorrectly staged artifacts). ## Motivation Air-gapped environments frequently have: no DNS resolution, blocked outbound egress, restricted IAM/no cloud credentials, and strict requirements for offline verification (checksums/signatures) prior to use. Prior `backup create` output was usable, but the workflow required manual copying and ad-hoc verification, and parts of the installer could still attempt network access depending on storage backend configuration. ## Design / Behavior - Bundle format: a directory containing `manifest.json` plus the encrypted payload(s) referenced by the manifest. The manifest includes: toolkit version, backup format version, created timestamp, file list, and SHA256 checksums per file. - `backup export --backup-id <id> --out <dir|tar>`: copies artifacts from the local cache/artifact store into the output bundle, writes/updates manifest checksums, and prints a copy-pasteable verification command. - `backup import --from <dir|tar> --into <cache>`: validates manifest schema, verifies checksums, enforces path traversal guards (no `..`, no absolute paths), and then stages files into the installer cache for subsequent `restore apply`. - `--offline` mode: disables any remote storage resolvers and fails fast if a backend requiring network is configured. Also disables AWS IMDS probing and any default credential chain that triggers metadata calls. - Local verification: `backup verify --bundle <dir>` (new subcommand) verifies checksums and prints a summary suitable for attaching to a ticket/escalation. ## Operator workflow example 1) On source site: `redwood-private-installer backup create --output s3://...` (or local) 2) Export: `redwood-private-installer backup export --backup-id 2025-02-06T021533Z --out ./redwood-backup-2025-02-06/` 3) Transfer directory via approved offline mechanism 4) On restore site (air-gapped): `redwood-private-installer backup import --from ./redwood-backup-2025-02-06/ --offline` 5) Restore: `redwood-private-installer restore apply --backup-id 2025-02-06T021533Z --offline` ## Implementation notes - Introduced `pkg/offline/bundle` helpers: manifest read/write, sha256 streaming, copy with fsync, atomic temp file writes. - Added `--offline` flag plumbing into the storage resolver layer; in offline mode we only permit `file://` URIs and local bundle sources. - Added explicit guardrails to prevent accidentally reading from `s3://` or `gs://` during import/verify when `--offline` is set. - Added unit tests for checksum verification, manifest schema validation, and path traversal rejection. - Added lightweight docs under `docs/airgapped-backup-restore.md` describing bundle layout, verification, and troubleshooting. ## Files / areas changed - `cmd/backup_export.go` (new) - `cmd/backup_import.go` (new) - `cmd/backup_verify.go` (new) - `pkg/offline/bundle/*` (new) - `pkg/storage/resolver.go` (offline gating) - `pkg/security/checksums.go` (sha256 helpers) - `docs/airgapped-backup-restore.md` (guidance + FAQ) - `docs/cli.md` (command reference updates) ## Testing - Unit: `go test ./...` includes new bundle tests - Manual: exported/imported bundle on a laptop with `REDWOOD_INSTALLER_OFFLINE=1` and verified no outbound calls (validated with `tcpdump` showing no SYNs, and by forcing DNS failure). - Negative tests: corrupted payload -> checksum mismatch; manifest missing file -> fails; malicious path `../../etc/passwd` -> rejected. ## Follow-ups (not included) - Bundle signing + signature verification (GPG/cosign) will be done in ENG-9829; this PR only covers checksums to close the immediate workflow gap. - Integrate `backup import` into the on-prem offline installer bundle (Release Engineering). ## Checklist - [x] No external calls in offline flow - [x] Checksum verification + clear operator output - [x] Docs for air-gapped workflow - [x] Tests for traversal + corruption cases

review_conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can we guarantee `--offline` doesn’t accidentally hit AWS IMDS via the default credential chain? We’ve been burned by this in CI and in locked-down customer networks (hangs ~2s per attempt).

Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Added explicit `DisableIMDS` toggle in the resolver when offline and a fast-fail if any non-file backend is configured. Also added a unit test that asserts offline mode rejects `s3://` even when creds exist.

Hanae Suzuki: Checksum verification is necessary but not sufficient for tamper resistance. Please make sure docs are clear that checksums only detect corruption unless the manifest is signed. Also: import must guard against path traversal / absolute paths.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated docs with a dedicated note: checksums detect corruption; signing is follow-up ENG-9829. Added path sanitation: reject absolute paths, `..` segments, and enforce extraction into a temp dir with atomic moves.

Fatima Noor: On-prem operators need a very explicit copy/paste verification command and a deterministic bundle layout. Also, can we support both directory and tarball? Some customers only allow moving a single file.

Benji Okafor (author): Added `--out <dir>` and `--out <file>.tar` support; same for `--from`. The CLI prints a suggested `backup verify --bundle ...` command and shows a short summary (bytes, file count, sha256 status).
Sean Gallagher: For SRE smoke tests, we’ll want a machine-readable verification report (json) so we can attach it to staging restore drill outputs. Can we add `--format json`?
Benji Okafor (author): Added `backup verify --format text|json` (default text). JSON output is a flat structure with per-file results; also includes `tool_version` and `backup_format_version`.
Connor O'Brien: CI failed on first run due to lint and an unused import; please fix and rerun. Also update `docs/cli.md` to include new subcommands.
Benji Okafor (author): Fixed lint, removed unused import, updated CLI docs. Re-ran CI (all green).
Hanae Suzuki: Security LGTM with the docs caveat + traversal guard.
Fatima Noor: LGTM; this unblocks the MedData-style air-gap flow. Please coordinate with Release Eng for the offline bundle packaging once ENG-9829 lands.
Connor O'Brien: Approved. Let’s make sure release notes call out the new commands and offline behavior.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Squash commit message: "Support air-gapped backup artifact import/export (offline mode + local checksum verification)"
